Let \((a,b,c)=(f(1),f(2),f(3))\).  
The conditions become:
- \(f(f(1))=f(a)\ge 1\), always true.
- \(f(f(2))=f(b)\ge 2\), so \(f(b)\in\{2,3\}\).
- \(f(f(3))=f(c)\ge 3\), so \(f(c)=3\).

Count triples \((a,b,c)\):

- If \(c=1\), then \(f(c)=3\Rightarrow a=3\). Need \(f(b)\ge 2\): valid \(b=1,2\), so \(2\) triples.
- If \(c=2\), then \(f(c)=3\Rightarrow b=3\). Then \(f(b)=f(3)=2\ge 2\), valid for all \(a\): \(3\) triples.
- If \(c=3\), then \(f(c)=3\) automatic. Need \(f(b)\ge 2\):
  - \(b=1\Rightarrow a=2,3\): \(2\)
  - \(b=2\): valid for all \(a\): \(3\)
  - \(b=3\): valid for all \(a\): \(3\)

Total: \(2+3+8=13\).

\[
\boxed{13}
\]
